Hey, nice work on the board! I reviewed the schematic and PCB files thoroughly, and they look solid overall. I only noticed a few points. Could you check them and let me know your thoughts?

1. USB-C connector (USB1) — The DRC reports hole clearance violations and negative annular width for the 2 mounting pin holes. It appears that the footprint’s drill is larger than its copper pad. Will JLCPCB accept that, or does it have to be corrected?
2. VMID (pin 36) on AXP2101 — On the PCB, it is tied to the same net as VSYS. VMID should be the internal ADC reference, so I would expect it to be isolated from VSYS with only a cap to GND. Could you verify this using the datasheet or a reference design?
3. R6 (4.7k) — It makes sense that the D1 LED is marked DNP, but R6, its current-limiting resistor, remains in the BOM and would be assembled. Because D1 will not be placed, one pin of R6 would float. Should R6 be marked DNP too, or is there a reason to retain it?
4. VSIS net name — This seems to be a typo for VSYS. It is only cosmetic, but correcting it would prevent confusion.
5. L1 inductor footprint — The DRC says that L\_Changjiang\_FTC404020S cannot be found in the standard KiCad library and that a local override is being used. I just want to verify that its physical dimensions match the 4.7uH inductor you intend to use.

The 22Ω resistors on SDA/SCL are only intended to improve signal quality. Because I2C lines are open-drain, releasing them requires the pull-up resistor to charge the cable capacitance back to 3.3V, which may produce a small overshoot or ringing at the transition edge. candidate_task.speaker: client
candidate_task.text:
The three boards form a chain: power board → main board → sensor board. Because the main board is in the middle, it receives power from the power board through J\_PWR\_PWR, uses that power locally, AND forwards it to the sensor board through J\_SENSOR\_PWR. It works like a power strip: power arrives through one cable, and the main board distributes it to both its own components and the sensor board through a second cable.
The INA219 is placed in-series on the 3.3V rail immediately after the Schottky diodes. It therefore gives one reading for the total 3.3V current consumed by everything downstream, including the ESP32 itself and anything drawn by the sensor board.

Therefore, none of the connected sensors requires the level shifter. You can omit it completely to free up board space. Should we need 5V-logic sensors in the future, we will use a small adapter board instead of permanently reserving footprints.

The three boards form a chain: power board → main board → sensor board. Because the main board is in the middle, it receives power from the power board through J\_PWR\_PWR, uses that power locally, AND forwards it to the sensor board through J\_SENSOR\_PWR.
